claims: The Artemis II Orion capsule splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California.
The Artemis II Orion capsule splashed down on Friday, April 10, 2026, at 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT).
The crew consisted of four astronauts.
The crew successfully completed a 10-day mission around the moon.
The crew was retrieved by US Navy divers.
The crew was transported via helicopter to the USS John P. Murtha.
Artemis II was the first crewed flight of the Artemis program.
Artemis II was designed as a test flight before future lunar landings.
Florida Today reported that this marked the successful conclusion of the 694,481-mile journey around the moon.
According to the official NASA blog, the crew is now undergoing post-mission medical evaluations.
